question: How is a bootstrap percentile interval for 95% confidence computed?
answer: A bootstrap percentile interval for 95% confidence is computed by using the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the B bootstrap statistics. [S1] This method does not require a formula for the standard error, making it useful for medians and other awkward statistics [S1].

citations.text:
3. The Bootstrap
The bootstrap estimates the uncertainty of a statistic by resampling. Draw n observations with
replacement from the original sample of size n, compute the statistic, and repeat this B times, for
example B = 1000. The spread of the B statistics approximates the sampling variability.
A bootstrap percentile interval for 95% confidence uses the 2.5th and the 97.5th percentiles of the
B bootstrap statistics. The bootstrap needs no formula for the standard error, which makes it useful
for medians and other awkward statistics.

S2.text: size grows. A confidence interval gives a range of plausible values for a parameter. A 95% confidence interval for  a mean with known sigma is x-bar plus or minus 1.96 * sigma / sqrt(n). When sigma is unknown and n is small, replace 1.96 with a critical value from the t distribution with n - 1 degrees of freedom. A 95% confidence level means that if the procedure were repeated many times, about 95% of the intervals would contain the true parameter; it does not mean there is a 95% probability that one specific computed interval contains it.

S3.title: Statistics Exercise Guide
S3.text:
Problem 3: Confidence Interval for a Mean
Question. A sample of n = 36 students has mean study time 12.4 hours per week. The population standard deviation is known to be 3 hours. Build a 95% confidence interval.
Solution. The standard error is 3 / sqrt(36) = 0.5. The margin of error is 1.96 * 0.5 = 0.98. The interval is 12.4 plus or minus 0.98, that is (11.42, 13.38). Interpretation: the procedure captures the true mean in about 95% of repeated samples. If the sample size were four times larger (n = 144) the standard error would halve to 0.25 and the interval would become narrower.

S5.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S5.text: 4. Sampling and Confidence Intervals A population is the entire group of interest and a sample is a subset used to learn about it. Simple random sampling gives every member an equal chance of selection; stratified sampling samples within subgroups; convenience sampling is easy but prone to bias. Sampling bias occurs when the sample systematically differs from the population. The sampling distribution of the mean describes how sample means vary from sample to sample. The Central Limit Theorem states that for sufficiently large n the distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal with mean mu and standard error sigma / sqrt(n), regardless of the shape of the original population.
